review: 1:1–1:2 מַה־לִּי פֹה … גֵר וְתוֹשָׁב — Psalm 39:13 (גֵּר אָנֹכִי עִמָּךְ תּוֹשָׁב) and Gen 23:4; the Arabic ضَيْفٌ غَرِيب ('a guest, a stranger') is that pair, and the Hebrew keeps both nouns.
3:2 מִיָּדִי לֹא יִנָּטֵל — 'it shall not be taken from my hand' (John 10:28, לֹא יַחְטֹף אִישׁ מִיָּדִי); the Arabic وَمِنْ يَدِي لَا يُنْزَعُ is the same assurance.

4:1 בְּהֵחָלֵץ הַזְּמָן — 'when time is over', for حِينَ يَنْتَهِي الزَّمَان; חָלַץ in the sense of drawing off/finishing is biblical (Lev 14:43 uses it of removing), and the niphal keeps the passive.

4:3–4:4 אַרְוֶה צְמָא שׁוֹקִי / שָׁם עִם הֶחָנוּן — 'I shall slake the thirst of my longing there with the Gracious One'; the Arabic أُرْوِي ظَمَا شَوْقِي … مَعْ ذَاكَ الْوَدُود is one sentence split across the couplet, and Hebrew keeps the split so the name lands last.
